title: Lunch on Saturday
subtitle: Emma and Jack don't cook on Saturday. They go out — and this is what you say.
description: An A1 reading and listening text set in an American restaurant: ordering, asking for the check, and tipping.
source: authored for this site; no source document
passage: On Saturday, Jack and I go out for lunch. We don't cook on Saturday.
We go to a small place near the park. It is not expensive and the food is good. We are hungry.
The server comes to our table. “Are you ready to order?”
“Yes,” I say. “I'd like the chicken sandwich, please. And a glass of water.”
“Can I have the chicken too? With rice, not fries.” Jack is always hungry.
The food comes in ten minutes. We eat and we talk. At the end, Jack asks for the check. It is twenty-four dollars. He pays, and he leaves a tip on the table.

exercises.title: Understanding the Text
exercises.instructions: Read again and choose the best answer.

items.prompt: Why do Emma and Jack eat in a restaurant on Saturday?
options: Because they don't cook on that day

items.prompt: What does Emma say about the price?
options: It does not cost a lot

items.prompt: What do Emma and Jack both eat?
items.explanation: Emma orders a chicken sandwich; Jack says “Can I have the chicken too?”

items.prompt: What does Jack not want with his food?

items.explanation: The server asks “Anything else?” and they say no.

items.prompt: What does Jack leave on the table?
items.explanation: He leaves a tip — extra money for the server. This is normal in the United States.
